composio.note: Composio manages OAuth for Zendesk, so prototypes need no own app. Use your own client for your branding on the consent screen.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio supplies a managed Zendesk app. For production you should bring your own app so users see your name, and you get dedicated quota and your own scopes.

prerequisites.title: Zendesk account on a plan with OAuth
prerequisites.detail: OAuth use is listed for Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise or Enterprise Plus (All Suites), and Team, Professional or Enterprise (Support). A Zendesk account is needed to get a client ID.

prerequisites.title: Admin permissions
prerequisites.detail: Creating and managing OAuth clients needs specific admin permissions in Admin Center.

steps.title: Create Zendesk OAuth client
steps.detail: In Admin Center go to Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients and add a client with name, identifier, client kind, redirect URLs and scopes. Copy the secret immediately; it is shown in full only once.
steps.done_when: You hold the client ID and the full client secret.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.detail: Draft the narrowest scopes, for example tickets:read instead of full read or write. Leaving scopes empty allows all of them.
steps.done_when: Scope list is ready to enter in the client form.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret. Use the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard in the Zendesk client.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Submit app for Zendesk review
steps.detail: Submit the app for Zendesk review and approval. A Marketplace profile is optional, and a first submission has its profile reviewed together with the app.

steps.title: Request global OAuth client
steps.detail: Request a global OAuth client so one app works across many Zendesk accounts. If it takes too long, email platformteam@zendesk.com.
steps.done_when: Zendesk grants the global OAuth client.

steps.title: Wait for Zendesk approval
steps.detail: No fixed timeline is documented for the review or the global OAuth request.

traps.title: Tokens expire and the user must re-authorize
traps.detail: Access tokens last 30 minutes by default (5 minutes to 48 hours). If a refresh token expires or is invalid, the user must go through the full authorization flow again.

traps.title: Authorization code lives only 120 seconds
traps.detail: Exchange the code for tokens quickly after redirect.

traps.title: Client secret shown only once
traps.detail: After saving, only the first nine characters remain visible, so store it right away.

traps.title: Expire tokens setting is permanent
traps.detail: Once enabled it cannot be turned off. Clients created after April 30, 2026 already have expirations by default.

traps.title: Use core subdomain and https redirects
traps.detail: The authorization URL needs the Zendesk core subdomain, not a host-mapped one. Redirect URLs must be https unless localhost or 127.0.0.1.

traps.title: Public clients require PKCE
traps.detail: Client kind must be Public or Confidential. Public clients must use PKCE; confidential clients can use PKCE, a secret, or both.

traps.title: Managed app limits
traps.detail: Managed apps show Composio's name, share quota across all Composio users, and use a 15-minute minimum polling interval.

blockers.symptom: Customers on API tokens cannot use your OAuth app
blockers.what_it_means: Customers using API-token apps must approve global OAuth once you make it available.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask each such customer's admin to approve global OAuth.

blockers.symptom: Global OAuth request pending for a long time
blockers.what_it_means: Duration depends on pending requests and time of week.
blockers.what_to_do: Email platformteam@zendesk.com if it takes longer than expected.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: To use OAuth authentication, you need to register your application with Zendesk.
evidence.answer: You must register your application with Zendesk to use OAuth authentication.

evidence.answer: The plan list on the page for Support includes Team, Professional, and Enterprise.

evidence.question: G1

evidence.answer: Creating and managing OAuth clients requires specific admin permissions; an admin who loses them no longer can manage the client, but the client stays active.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Click Add OAuth client on the right side of the OAuth client list.
evidence.answer: Registering an OAuth client is a manual step done by an admin in Admin Center, not an automatic registration.

evidence.question: G2

evidence.answer: The standard OAuth client setup described on the page is for users of one Zendesk account.

evidence.question: G2

evidence.answer: Apps that interact with many Zendesk accounts can request a global OAuth client instead.

evidence.answer: The read scope gives an app access to GET endpoints, including permission to sideload related resources.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.answer: The write scope gives an app access to POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints for creating, updating, and deleting resources.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.answer: The impersonate scope lets a Zendesk admin make requests on behalf of end users.

evidence.answer: Scopes can be narrowed to specific resources, such as tickets:read to only read tickets.

evidence.answer: When registering the client, the admin selects the scopes the client can request; leaving the field empty allows all scopes.

evidence.question: G5

evidence.answer: Authorization codes are valid for only 120 seconds.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: The default, minimum, and maximum expiration times are:
evidence.answer: Access tokens have a default lifetime of 30 minutes, a minimum of 5 minutes, and a maximum of 48 hours.

evidence.question: G5

evidence.answer: If a refresh token expires or is invalid, the user must go through the full authorization flow again.

evidence.answer: The Expire tokens setting cannot be turned off once enabled; it applies a default expiration to all tokens issued by the client.

evidence.question: G5

evidence.answer: For OAuth clients created after April 30, 2026, the Expire tokens checkbox is disabled because those clients already have expirations set by default.

evidence.answer: The page lists the plan tiers that include OAuth use but does not state any prices, credits, or fees.

evidence.answer: The end user, not an admin, is sent to the Zendesk authorization page to grant the app access on their behalf.

evidence.answer: The Zendesk authorization page opens in the end user's browser.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Other users can also continue to authorize the application and obtain new
evidence.answer: Other users can also authorize the application and obtain new tokens, and their tokens act on behalf of the individual user who authorized it.

evidence.question: G9

evidence.answer: The redirect URI must be secure (https) unless the app uses localhost or 127.0.0.1.

evidence.question: G9

evidence.answer: The authorization URL uses the Zendesk core subdomain, not a host-mapped subdomain.

evidence.answer: Requests to the token endpoint must be over https and formatted as JSON.

evidence.answer: To create the client, go to Apps and integrations in the Admin Center sidebar, then select APIs > OAuth clients.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: Required setup fields include Name, Identifier, Client kind, Redirect URLs, and Scopes, plus optional Description, Company, and Logo.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Identifier - The field is auto-populated with a reformatted version of the
evidence.answer: The Identifier field is auto-populated from the app name and can be changed.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: The client kind must be set to Public or Confidential.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: These clients are required to use PKCE.
evidence.answer: Public clients are required to use PKCE.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: These clients can use PKCE, client secret, or both.
evidence.answer: Confidential clients can use PKCE, a client secret, or both.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Setting the kind property is mandatory for all new OAuth clients created
evidence.answer: Setting the client kind is mandatory for new OAuth clients created in Admin Center.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: The logo image can be a JPG, GIF, or PNG file.

evidence.answer: After saving, a pre-populated Secret field appears that holds the client secret.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: The full secret is displayed only once; after saving, only the first nine characters are visible.

evidence.question: G10

evidence.answer: The unique identifier from the registered client is used as the client_id in API calls.

evidence.answer: The page gives no numeric threshold of users, workspaces, or installs before an app can be used or listed; it only mentions the global OAuth client option for many Zendesk accounts.

items.reason: Quote states internal-use customers are not impacted and third-party developers must meet new standards.
Quote says the section describes OAuth client setup for users of one Zendesk account; 'standard' is a minor addition.
Quote says all apps built for distribution to customers, listed or not, must be submitted for review and approval.
Quote says all public integrations will be required to go through Marketplace review.
Quote says Zendesk requires third-party developers to complete enhanced Zendesk security reviews.
Quote says it is difficult to say how long a request takes, depending on pending requests and time of week; no fixed timeline is given.
Quote says developers can request a global OAuth client.
Quote says the marketplace app ecosystem goes through a review ensuring apps can be trusted; the quotes list no specific checks, consistent with the statement.
Quote says API-token customers must approve the new global OAuth method when the developer makes it available.
Quote says app developers must conform to rules on handling customer data so it is not misused or exposed.
Quote says Zendesk must not be referenced as announcing the news of an app, partnership, or integration.
Quote gives an example parameter restricting an app to only reading tickets.
Quote says to select the scopes the client can request, but does not say an empty field allows all scopes.
Quote says a profile is optional and is published only after app approval, so it is not a required step.
Quote says a first-time submission has the profile reviewed together with the app or theme.
Quote says if a request takes longer than expected, the developer can email platformteam@zendesk.com.
Quote only introduces a table of default, minimum and maximum expiration times; the values themselves are not in the quotes.
Quote is truncated at 'send the user through the', so it is cut off before stating the full authorization flow requirement.
Quote states the authorization code is only valid for 120 seconds.
Quote states the setting is permanent and cannot be turned off once enabled.
Quote says clients already have expirations set by default, but the April 30, 2026 date and disabled checkbox are not in the quotes.
Quotes say internal-use apps are not impacted by the changes, which implies no new review, but do not explicitly state that no provider review is needed.
Quotes cover the one-account OAuth client section and plans, but do not state the admin registration step in the Admin Center or the order of steps.
Quotes support the plan requirement (Team, Professional, Enterprise and others) and the need for a Zendesk account, but do not mention an Admin role.
Quotes state apps for distribution to customers and public integrations must go through Zendesk review and approval.
Quotes state all distributed apps and all public integrations must be submitted for review, with no exception given.
Quotes support the review submission, but do not give the full ordered sequence (register client, submit, request global OAuth, wait for approval).
Quote states API-token customers will need to approve the new global OAuth method.
Quotes state the customer data handling rules and the rule that Zendesk must not be referenced as announcing news.
Quotes support the hardest case (multi-customer distribution needing review and global OAuth, with unpredictable wait), but do not give the 'about 1 hour' or 'no wait' for the easiest case.
